root_cause_label: Shallow Behavioral Analysis Without Proper Decompilation
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent chose to approximate the ray-tracer's output using guessed gradient and checkerboard heuristics instead of reverse-engineering the actual algorithm, and then declared success despite differing pixel values.
t_err_evidence: cat > /app/mystery.c ... sky gradient and ground checker pattern, wrong algorithm committed
t_commit_evidence: Step 24 is both the error and commit point: once the agent commits to an approximation strategy (iterating heuristic C code rather than decompiling), it never departs from this approach for the remaining 15 steps, making a correct outcome impossible.
trigger_explanation: The agent assumed that sampling a handful of boundary pixel values (sky colors at a few rows, ground gray values) was sufficient to reconstruct the exact rendering algorithm, without verifying whether a simple linear gradient and bit-shift checker could reproduce per-pixel values. This unverified assumption drove the entire implementation strategy.
forewarning_evidence: R:Row G:1: B:159 R:Row G:201: B:159 — garbled pixel output from awk misparsing
